terms.gloss: so that, in order to; so that … not
terms.grammar: conjunctions, with the present subjunctive after a present or future main verb, the imperfect after a past one
evidence: Ov. Ars 2.107: ut amēris, amābilis estō
Quint. 6.1.46: date puerō pānem, nē plōret
terms.comment: English “to …” of purpose is a clause in Latin, never a bare infinitive: vēnī ut tē vidērem. A purpose to be avoided takes nē, not ut nōn; “and so that … not” is nēve.

terms.grammar: conjunction, where the clause has a comparative
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.97: respondisse sē, quō melius cēnāret, obsōnāre ambulandō famem

terms.grammar: the supine in -um after a verb of motion
evidence: Hor. S. 1.5.48: lūsum it Maecēnās, dormītum ego Vergiliusque
terms.comment: “Go and sleep”, “come to eat”: dormītum īre, cēnātum venīre. The gerund with ad or causā does the same work: see purpose.

phrases.english: Let’s go in and have lunch.
give the boy some bread, so that he doesn’t cry
Hold me, please, so I don’t fall.

phrases.latin: Sōcratēn ferunt … respondisse sē, quō melius cēnāret, obsōnāre ambulandō famem
phrases.english: they say Socrates answered that he was buying in hunger by walking, so as to dine better

phrases.latin: lūsum it Maecēnās, dormītum ego Vergiliusque
phrases.english: Maecenas goes off to play, Virgil and I to sleep
